content.jointProblem: Can uncertainty-aware spatial exposure modelling link incompletely geocoded farm policies to hail estimates and identify potentially underpriced portfolio segments more reliably than municipality-level loading? A first experiment would test whether the available location and weather data support field-level inference, and whether transferring spatial-extremes and Bayesian pricing methods improves held-out claims prediction and calibration without implying unsupported spatial precision.

rationale.text: He has directly relevant Bayesian insurance-pricing experience, including credibility weighting and quarterly model updating, although the demonstrated application is motor telematics rather than hail.

sources.quote: classic credibility estimators can be embedded in a Bayesian linear model with conjugate normal–inverse-gamma priors.
outlines a procedure for updating the model quarterly as new data arrive.

rationale.text: His work on spatial dependence in extreme events provides a methodological starting point for modelling geographically concentrated hail exposure, subject to validation on hail data.

sources.quote: A spatial analysis using a max-stable process model reveals a correlation range of approximately 2.1 km

rationale.text: He leads probabilistic modelling and uncertainty quantification for agricultural sensor networks in the same region.

sources.quote: Struhár leads the work package on probabilistic modelling and uncertainty quantification, contributing Gaussian process and Bayesian hierarchical methods tailored to irregular and energy-constrained sampling schedules.

rationale.text: He has practical property-insurance consulting experience spanning model specification, data pipelines and regulatory documentation.

sources.quote: a sensor-based premium adjustment scheme for commercial fire risk, covering model specification, data pipeline requirements, and regulatory documentation.

rationale.text: His project experience includes interpretable Bayesian risk pipelines designed for organisations without dedicated data-science teams.

sources.quote: extracting interpretable statistical features, and fitting hierarchical Bayesian risk models suitable for small and medium enterprises that lack dedicated data science teams.

constraints.text: Policy-to-field matching must resolve or explicitly propagate settlement-level location uncertainty; a settlement centroid cannot be treated as a verified insured field.

sources.quote: a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: Field-level hail estimates must be supportable from the available weather observations; finer model output alone cannot overcome coarse spatial and temporal inputs.

sources.quote: We do receive daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution
a storm can devastate one village and leave the farm two kilometres away untouched.

constraints.text: Initial estimation and validation must respect the limited historical sample and avoid treating policies affected by the same storm as independent validation observations.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.

constraints.text: The deliverable must include an automated route into the existing quarterly Python pricing workflow, rather than stopping at a GIS map.

sources.quote: turning that into something that feeds the pricing model automatically is beyond what our team can do alone.
Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh

constraints.text: Implementation and maintenance must fit the company's shared operational staffing capacity.

sources.quote: a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.

constraints.text: Plan formal data-sharing arrangements before transferring policy and claims records, consistent with the researcher's stated collaboration preference.

sources.quote: He prefers collaborations where data-sharing agreements can be established formally; his department has a standard template for this.

risks: There is a material transfer gap: the demonstrated spatial-extremes method concerns water-network pressure, agricultural models concern microclimate and disease, and pricing validation concerns motor telematics—not hail losses. The first experiment must test these transfers rather than assume them.
Daily five-kilometre weather grids and settlement-only addresses may make defensible field-level hail reconstruction impossible without additional observations or parcel information.
Three claim years may contain too few independent hailstorms to estimate tail losses or demonstrate stable pricing improvements; random policy splits could exaggerate performance.
The reported 18% excess does not establish hail-exposure mismeasurement as its cause; insured values, coverage, claims handling and loss inflation may also matter.
Researcher availability and committed joint-project effort are unknown. Budget, delivery deadline, weather-data usage rights and company acceptance requirements are also unknown.
Integration could stall under shared staffing constraints; the company's earlier flood-mapping prototype was completed but has not entered the pricing system.
questions: What joint-project effort can the researcher commit, and who will own geospatial engineering, actuarial validation and production integration?
Can insured assets be linked to verified coordinates or cadastral parcels, and do loss geotags identify the damaged asset rather than a settlement or reporting address?

What exactly does MeteoVoj provide about hail, with what timestamps, uncertainty and historical coverage? Are radar, station, satellite or independent hail-footprint observations accessible and licensed for this use?
Are policy-year exposure records available for both claimed and unclaimed policies, including insured values, deductibles, coverage changes, claim dates and claim development?

Can the first experiment reserve entire storms, locations and a season for validation, compare against municipality loading, and agree prediction, calibration and spatial-resolution acceptance criteria before modelling?
What budget, deadline and company staff allocation are available, including any funding needed for supplementary weather data or geocoding?
What data-protection, pricing-explainability and regulatory approvals apply, and can the parties execute the researcher's formal data-sharing agreement?
What interface, monitoring, approval and maintenance requirements must an automated pricing output satisfy, and what prevented integration of the earlier flood-risk tool?
